idiom_name: *TableModule class over JdbcTemplate result lists (or jOOQ Table records)
implementation_notes: Java has no platform record set, so the module is a hand-written class per table whose methods return List<Map<String, Object>> (JdbcTemplate.queryForList) or List<Record> (jOOQ) and whose write side uses set-oriented SQL through update/batchUpdate. jOOQ gets closest to the pattern with generated Table/Record types giving one table-typed API per table and compile-checked queries, while Spring's JdbcTemplate keeps the row carrier completely untyped. Because JPA/Hibernate is the dominant persistence style and maps rows to entities, a JPA-centric stack pulls the design toward Domain Model or Active Record; choose Table Module deliberately where the logic really is set-shaped (batch, import, reconciliation) and keep the SQL in one place.
pitfalls: List<Map<String, Object>> loses column types, and a SQL NULL becomes an indistinguishable absent-or-null entry; route rows through a row mapper or a record type per table as soon as the module has more than a couple of operations.

JdbcTemplate calls run in their own transaction unless the caller supplies one: the module's rules must be invoked inside a @Transactional/TransactionTemplate boundary or a multi-table rule commits partially.
